Definition: Eder, the name of an Israelite and of two places in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Eder is the name of a Merarite Levite in David's day and of two towns, one in the far south of Judah and one named in the lists beside it. The Levite is counted among the sons of Mushi who served in the temple, and the towns sit on the border of Edom, at the edge of the inheritance. The same name covers a man who served and places that marked the boundary.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that serving God and marking His boundaries both matter, because the Levite kept the worship going and the towns kept the land. Eder's name, flock, fits both: a people kept and a place kept.
